assessments.reasoning: GNU's edition-specific plaintext supplies the title, version and month in the controlled opening range [0,92). The source role and the claim both concern the publisher's identification of this edition.

challenge.method: Tested whether the family title on a neighboring edition, the Addendum's sample header, or an authorized work notice selecting 1.1 could establish the same publisher identity and printed date.
challenge.results: A neighboring edition can share the family title while carrying a different version number. The sample illustrates a possible grant, and an actual work notice can select 1.1. Neither establishes what version and month GNU printed at the head of this instrument. The acquired heading supplies both.

limitations: March 2000 is the printed edition date. The claim record describes active as a proposed index lifecycle state. The heading supplies no evidence for that administrative designation.
The heading and governing-permission acquisitions resolve to the same GNU URL and body digest. They supply one publisher source.
reasoning: The opening heading in the separate publisher-heading acquisition names the GNU Free Documentation License and prints Version 1.1 and March 2000 together. This directly identifies the edition in revision 1.
